title: Private deploy commitment calendar & initiative slice playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: produce a single-quarter commitment calendar and a reproducible playbook for slicing Private/VPC/On‑Prem initiatives into sprint-aligned deliverables. This ticket captures scope, acceptance criteria, stakeholder cadence, risk gates, and the handoffs required to convert large enterprise asks into ship-ready sprint commitments.

Why now: multiple customers are asking for deterministic timelines for Private deployments and predictable upgrade windows. We need a prescriptive mechanism to translate OKRs into coordinated inter-team slices (engineering, infra, security, CE, legal) so commercial promises match engineering commitments.

Scope: define a repeatable quarterly planning template (calendar view + sprint buckets), define tranche gating criteria (compatibility, infra readiness, audit sign-off), draft runbook templates for each rollout lane (canary -> cohort -> general), map out required artifacts (PRD, compliance checklist, migration playbook), and produce a public-facing customer commitment calendar for AE/CS teams.

Out of scope: implementation of autoscaler itself (tracked in ENG-84210) and detailed infra capacity calculations per-customer (those remain in customer-specific scoping tickets).

Deliverables: 1) Commitment calendar template (GCal + CSV) that maps initiatives to sprint windows and delivery owners. 2) Initiative slice playbook (one-page runbook per slice) including rollback triggers, test acceptance criteria, and contact roster. 3) Stakeholder sync cadence and escalation paths. 4) Updated Console release/process dashboard to show cohort windows (low-fi mock for Q2 runway).

Acceptance criteria and signals of readiness are listed below. Links to the PRD and mockups added under attachments.
acceptance_criteria: Commitment calendar template created and reviewed by Eng, Security, CE, and Sales
Playbook runbook draft published in Confluence with rollback triggers and audit checklist
Three sample initiative slices mapped from current backlog and timeboxed to sprints
Stakeholder cadence scheduled (weekly PM-Eng sync + biweekly exec review) and invited attendees confirmed
Customer-facing commitment calendar exported and validated with two pilot accounts (legal & CS sign-off)
tasks: Draft calendar template and ingest existing Q1 initiative dates
Workshop with Eng leads to align sprint buckets and identify hard dependencies
Work with Security to define minimal audit gating criteria and sign-off flow
Create two pilot tranches and run a tabletop canary exercise with Ops/CE
Publish playbook and share with AE/CS for pilot commitments
metrics: % of private deals with committed delivery windows >= 90%
Mean deviation between committed window and actual delivery (target <= 7 days)
Number of rollout regressions per tranche (target 0 for pilot)
Time from commitment to first canary (target <= 30 days)
CS satisfaction score for delivery predictability (target >= 4.2/5)
decisions: Split large initiatives into sprint-sized 'slices' tied to explicit acceptance tests
Require Security sign-off at slice B1 (pre-canary) and again at general availability gate
Use a two-cohort canary (internal + 1 pilot customer) before broad rollouts
Expose a read-only commitment calendar to AE/CS to reduce ad-hoc SLAs
notes: Trade-off: stricter gating reduces risk but increases lead time; aim for measurable windows to balance both
We will not lock capacity in this playbook; capacity commitments will be negotiated separately with Dedicated sales
Design team will produce low-fidelity console widget to visualize 'commitment lanes' for Q2 prototype
Engineering requests: attach ENG-84210 and ETA on autoscaler mock to properly size sprint buckets
